Wake vortices result from lift and trail behind aircraft as two counter-rotating vortices.
ICAO currently imposes conservative wake vortex separation minima limiting airport capacity.
RECAT-EU program aims to optimize wake vortex separation using aircraft categories and weather-dependent procedures.
Wake vortex circulation Γ is defined as Γ = Mg / (ρ V b), where M is aircraft weight, ρ air density, V aircraft speed, and b vortex separation.
Vortex descent speed V is approximated by Γ / (2π b).
Wake vortices decay in two phases: initial viscous dissipation followed by enhanced decay due to turbulence.
Ground effect influences vortex rebound, strength asymmetry, and secondary vortex generation.
Radar backscatter from wake vortices in clear air is caused by Bragg scattering from refractive index fluctuations.
The refractive index depends on air density, water vapor content, and temperature, modeled by Thayer's formula.
Radar cross-section (RCS) is computed by coupling Navier-Stokes flow simulations with Maxwell electromagnetic scattering equations.
The Born approximation is used to simplify electromagnetic scattering calculations.
Simulations use Reynolds number Re = 5000 and Brunt–Väisälä frequency N ≈ 0.01 s⁻¹ for moderate stratification.
Radar Doppler signatures characterize vortex roll-up geometry and velocity distribution.
Rainy weather radar simulations incorporate raindrop concentration and scattering effects to model radar signatures.
Field trials at Paris Charles de Gaulle airport support RECAT-EU deployment.
Radar detection can localize wake vortices in range, azimuth, and elevation with high Doppler resolution (~0.2 m/s).
Wake vortex encounters mostly occur below 100 feet and between 3500-4500 feet altitude.
Radar trials have detected wake vortices with RCS values around −65 to −80 dBm² in S and C bands.
The radar model was validated against analytical sphere RCS results and Kwajalein experimental data.
Dynamic pair-wise separation minima based on radar detection and weather data can increase airport throughput safely.
